proctor-prediction.notes: v2 best: XGBoost + SHAP interaction features (NMAE=0.2548). v3: PINN with ZAV saturation + air-voids physics loss; ablation over λ_ZAV ∈ {0,0.5,1,5,10} + ensemble with XGBoost. Requires KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE; uses MPS (Apple Silicon). v5 plan added 2026-07-02: SINDy sparse symbolic feature discovery + SHAP-guided refinement (materializing v2's redundant-pair/interaction findings) + GBM/PINN stacked ensemble. Target: beat v1's 0.2431 CV NMAE. v5 implemented 2026-07-02: SINDy (STLSQ static sparse symbolic regression, repurposed from dynamical-systems use) discovered 21 nonlinear feature terms; SHAP refinement dropped 11 redundant raw/log PSD cols and materialized 10 interaction product features (acting on v2 findings that were never applied); Optuna-tuned XGBoost (0.2441) blended 0.8/0.2 with a PINN diversity model (0.2776 alone) beat both individually and the Ridge-meta-learner alternative (0.2575): final CV NMAE 0.2410, new best. Required pinning OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 etc. before importing xgboost/lightgbm/shap/torch together in one process -- otherwise the run deadlocks at PINN training (first version to combine GBM and PINN in a single kernel). Updated 2026-07-02 15:15 to reuse helper_functions.py (calc_satline, get_missing_data_report) per user request; verified mathematically behavior-neutral (calc_satline is the identical ZAV formula, incl. on torch tensors) and re-validated end-to-end -- CV NMAE 0.2420, still beats v1. load_and_summarize_data was tried but doesn't fit this repo's split data/ + root sample_submission.csv layout, so skipped. v6 (2026-07-02): scripts/v6.py wires organizers' helper_functions.py into a full leak-free CV pipeline (fold-isolated MICE + ExtraTrees/HistGB/Ridge/PINN registry, random/Optuna tuning, ensemble prediction, saturation clip); produced submissions/submission_20260702_1438_v6.csv but CV NMAE was never logged to model_description.md -- infrastructure upgrade, no new model family. v7 plan added 2026-07-06: standalone KNN diversity model (plan.md §12) -- reuse v5's SINDy+SHAP feature set, scale features (new requirement vs. tree models), sweep k/weights/metric per target, report standalone CV NMAE first, then test OOF-blend value against v5's GBM+PINN mix (0.2410 fixed blend) -- ship only if the blend beats it, otherwise document as a negative result per v2's precedent. v7 design added 2026-07-06 (design.md §11): user requested clay/silt/sand/gravel/fine-grained/ip columns -- checked against existing feature set: sand/gravel/ip are duplicates of already-existing feat_sand_pct/feat_gravel_pct/feat_pi (reuse, don't duplicate); clay is an alias of the raw psd_passing_at_0_002mm_pct column; only silt (passing_0.063 - passing_0.002) and fine_grained boolean (clay+silt>12, renamed from hyphenated 'fine-grained' which isn't a valid identifier) are genuinely new. Flagged that clay+silt+sand+gravel sum to exactly 100% (compositional, linear recombination of the 3 raw PSD passing-% cols already in NUMERIC_COLS) -- fine for tree models but double-counts fines-content signal in KNN's distance metric if both raw and decomposed forms are kept; recommend using one representation only, or re-validate via SHAP before keeping both, mirroring v2/v5's redundant-pair handling. v7 implemented 2026-07-06 (scripts/v7.py, imports v6.py directly): design correction found only fine_grained was genuinely new (clay/silt/sand/gravel/ip already existed as psd_fraction_clay/silt/sand/gravel + atterberg_plasticity_index in helper_functions.py); added fine_grained flag plus a KNN candidate family (24-config sweep: n_neighbors x weights x metric) run inside v6's CV registry for fold-aligned OOF. Found and worked around a v6.py bug: run_cv_pipeline's per-fold table computes IQR per-fold (~40 rows) instead of the fixed global IQR the plan/design docs require -- v7 scores model selection from OOF arrays against the fixed global IQR instead. Result: KNN not competitive alone (0.3470 vs ExtraTrees 0.2517 OOF NMAE; manhattan >> euclidean for this feature set); blend (0.95 ExtraTrees + 0.05 KNN) only reaches 0.2515, a 0.0002 'improvement' within noise of the blend-weight grid search itself, and v6's own base pipeline (0.2517) doesn't beat v5's 0.2410-0.2420 anyway. Per plan.md's own acceptance criteria this doesn't beat v5 -- documented as a negative result in model_description.md v7 section; v5 remains the project's best. submissions/submission_20260706_v7.csv regenerated and kept for reference per explicit follow-up request (2026-07-06) even though it should not be used as the competition entry. Follow-up (2026-07-06): added soil-composition-stratified CV folds to v7.py per user request -- v1-v6 used plain shuffled KFold, which at n=201 can by chance skew a fold's clay/silt/sand/gravel mix. v7.py buckets samples into dominant DIN fraction (Sand/Gravel/Fine, Clay merged into Fine since train.csv has only 1 clay-dominant sample and StratifiedKFold needs >= n_splits per class) and uses StratifiedKFold instead; v6.py itself left unmodified (added run_cv_pipeline_stratified in v7.py, a copy of v6.run_cv_pipeline's body with pluggable fold source, rather than touching v6's shared function). Re-ran: ExtraTrees 0.2497 (was 0.2517), KNN blend 0.2493 (was 0.2515) -- slightly better, more representative CV estimate, but conclusion unchanged: still doesn't beat v5's 0.2410-0.2420, still a negative result.
